pages.q: Is Chandler, AZ a good place to rent an apartment?
pages.short: For many renters, yes. Chandler is an East Valley city with freeway access across the metro, a large tech and finance job base in the Price Corridor, downtown dining and major shopping centers. South Chandler, where Village of Chandler sits near Ocotillo and Loop 202, offers a peaceful neighborhood feel while keeping those conveniences close.

p: Chandler is part of the Phoenix metro, and its location is one of the reasons people choose it. The city's own Price Corridor business district sits where Loop 101 and Loop 202 meet, and the city lists Intel, Wells Fargo, Bank of America, Northrop Grumman and Microchip Technology among its notable employers there.
Downtown Chandler is known for its dining, and Chandler Fashion Center gives you a large shopping option close to home.
Everyday convenience is easy to find too. Ocotillo Golf Club and San Tan Village Mall are near south Chandler, and the freeways make it simple to reach work or weekend plans across the Valley.
bullets: Freeway access to Gilbert, Mesa and Phoenix
A large tech and finance job base
Downtown dining, shopping centers and golf nearby

sections.h: What to think about before you sign
p: Like the rest of the Valley, Chandler summers are very hot, so cooling costs and shade matter. Traffic on the main freeways has grown over the years, so test your commute at the hours you would actually drive it.
Rents vary by neighborhood and home type. Compare the full monthly cost, not just base rent, since many communities add required monthly services.

Village of Chandler is at 6075 S Gilbert Rd in south Chandler, near Ocotillo with quick access to Loop 202 and Gilbert Road. It offers townhome style apartments in one, two and three bedroom plans, each with private yard living, smart locks and an in unit washer and dryer.
For starting rents, specials and the full monthly cost, see the Village of Chandler leasing guide on MoveInLocal, or call the leasing team at 480 366 4682.

pages.q: What is the difference between a townhome style apartment and a regular apartment?
pages.short: A townhome style apartment gives you a layout that feels more like a house, often with fewer shared walls, more privacy and outdoor space of your own, while you still rent from a managed community with a leasing team, maintenance and shared amenities. A regular apartment is usually a unit in a larger building with shared hallways or stairwells.

sections.h: How townhome style living feels different
p: The biggest difference is how private your home feels day to day. Townhome style homes tend to have their own entry and outdoor space instead of a door off a shared corridor. At Village of Chandler, every home comes with private yard living, and select homes have enclosed backyards and detached layouts.

Space is the other big difference. Village of Chandler plans range from a one bedroom with about 679 square feet to a three bedroom, three bath plan with about 1,350 square feet, and the two bedroom, two bath plan has about 996 square feet. The two and three bedroom plans have as many baths as bedrooms, which can make sharing a home with a roommate easier.

sections.h: What you keep from apartment living
p: You still rent from a professionally managed community, so you get a leasing team, maintenance requests and shared amenities. At Village of Chandler that includes a resort style pool, an outdoor fitness center, a dog park, gas grills, green courtyards, a cornhole lawn and community Wi Fi. Assigned covered parking is included, and detached garages are available for an added monthly cost.

pages.q: How can I keep my summer electric bill down in an Arizona apartment?
pages.short: Set your thermostat higher, use ceiling fans, change your air filter often and shift heavy chores like laundry to off peak hours if your plan rewards it. SRP, a major Valley utility, recommends 78 to 80 degrees while you are home and up to 85 degrees while you are away, plus changing air filters about once a month.

p: Small changes add up over a long Arizona summer. SRP suggests these steps:
bullets: Set the thermostat to 78 to 80 degrees when home
Let it rise to as high as 85 degrees when you are away
Run ceiling fans so they push air downward, and turn them off when you leave the room, since fans cool people, not rooms
Change your air filter about once a month

p: Some Arizona electric plans charge different rates by time of day. SRP notes that customers who can shift chores like laundry to off peak hours can save money each month. Find out which plan your home is on before you set your routine.

Keep blinds and curtains closed on sunny windows during the day. SRP notes they help, but they work best as a backup to other steps, since they block heat after it reaches the glass. Keeping vents clear of furniture also helps your system run efficiently.

pages.q: Do I pay city rental tax on my apartment rent in Chandler, AZ?
pages.short: No, not for rent periods after December 31, 2024. According to the Arizona Department of Revenue, a 2023 change to state law prohibits Arizona cities and towns, including Chandler, from taxing residential rentals, and the city rental tax ended as of January 1, 2025. If you see a city rental tax line on a Chandler lease, ask the leasing team about it.

p: For years, many Arizona cities charged a transaction privilege tax on residential rent, and landlords often passed it on to renters. The Arizona Department of Revenue explains that state law was amended (Laws 2023, Chapter 204) to prohibit a city, town or other taxing jurisdiction from taxing residential rentals from and after December 31, 2024. Owners were told to stop collecting city rental tax starting January 1, 2025.

sections.h: What that means for your monthly cost
p: The rental tax line is gone, but that does not mean rent is the only monthly cost. Many communities list required monthly services separately from rent. Read the full fee list before you sign so you know your real monthly total.

Comparing communities is easier when you line up the same items for each one: base rent, fixed monthly services, usage based utilities, parking, pets and any one time move in costs. That gives you a true side by side number instead of comparing headline rents.
bullets: Ask for the full list of required monthly fees
Ask which utilities are billed by usage
Ask about optional items like garages or pet rent

pages.q: How much can an Arizona landlord charge for a security deposit, and when do I get it back?
pages.short: Under Arizona's Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, a landlord cannot demand more than one and one half months' rent as security, including prepaid rent. After the tenancy ends, you return possession and you ask for your deposit, the landlord has fourteen days, not counting weekends and legal holidays, to send an itemized list of deductions and any refund.

bullets: Limit: no more than one and one half months' rent, including prepaid rent, though a tenant may choose to pay more rent in advance
Return: within fourteen days, excluding weekends and legal holidays, after the tenancy ends, you deliver possession and you make a demand
Deductions must be itemized, with the amount due to you
Nonrefundable fees must have their purpose stated in writing; any fee or deposit not labeled nonrefundable is refundable
p: These rules come from the security deposit section of the Arizona Revised Statutes (Title 33, section 1321). This is general information, not legal advice.

Take date stamped photos of every room and the yard when you move in, and again when you move out. Report any existing damage in writing early. Leave a forwarding address, since the itemized list is normally mailed to your last known address unless you agree otherwise in writing.

Keep a copy of your signed lease, your move in condition notes and any written repair requests in one place. If there is a disagreement at move out, that record makes it much easier to sort out. Cleaning the home well and returning all keys, remotes and access devices also helps you avoid deductions.

pages.q: How do apartment move in specials work in Chandler, and how do I get one?
pages.short: Move in specials are discounts a community offers, often on select homes or floor plans, to fill openings. They change often, may apply only to certain homes, lease terms or move in dates, and should be confirmed in writing in your lease. Specials at Village of Chandler change, so check the leasing guide and ask which homes qualify.

p: A special might lower your effective cost over the lease, but the details matter. Some apply only to certain homes, plans or move in dates. Some are spread across the lease, and others apply up front.

Specials are most common when a community has several homes open at once or when a floor plan has extra availability. Because they can change quickly, ask about specials when you call and again when you tour, and confirm the terms before you commit to a home.
bullets: Ask which exact homes qualify
Ask how the special is applied to your rent
Ask whether it depends on lease length or a move in date
Get the terms in writing in your lease
